primitives.name: Visual Attention Hierarchy
primitives.verbatim_quote: --description: Strengthen the "do this first" visual hierarchy allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash(git diff*), Bash(git log*), Bash(git status*) --Evaluate the cockpit's visual hierarchy: when the owner opens it, is the single most important action unmistakable within ~2 seconds?
primitives.assumptions: Attention distribution is normalized; primary action must exceed secondary actions by threshold S > 0.5.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A_primary < A_secondary, visual hierarchy fails.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian belief update maps to GSE state transition via salient action selection.
layer2.telemetry: User click-through rate on primary anchor vs. secondary elements.

primitives.name: Primary Anchor Dominance
primitives.verbatim_quote: Propose one clear primary anchor (size, color, position, or motion) and de-emphasize secondary blocks.
primitives.assumptions: Dominance increases monotonically with size, color contrast, and motion magnitude.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D < 1, anchor fails to dominate attention field.

layer2.mapping: GSE motion and positioning kernel drives GSI perceptual salience model.
layer2.telemetry: Eye-tracking fixation duration on primary anchor vs. control group.

primitives.name: Attention Competition Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Attention currently competes between the posture medallion (`apps/web/app/cockpit/page.tsx` — `PostureMedallion`, the gate-fill ring), the Decision Queue (`apps/web/app/cockpit/page.tsx`), and the Company pulse (`apps/web/components/cockpit/cockpit-pulse.tsx` — `CockpitPulse`).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_i': 'Attention share of item i (dimensionless)', 'N': 'Number of competing items (dimensionless)', 'C_{ij}': 'Competition coefficient between items i,j (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each item receives normalized attention such that ΣA_i = 1; C_ij ∈ [0,1].
primitives.breakdown_regime: When max(A_i) < 1/N, competition leads to cognitive overload.

layer2.mapping: GSI multi-armed bandit models compete for attention; GSE state machine tracks conflict resolution.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-decision under varying numbers of competing UI elements.

reasoning_traces.think:
The visual attention hierarchy primitive defines a mathematical framework where user focus is directed toward a single dominant action within a defined temporal window T. The system assumes that attention is distributed among competing UI components, modeled as a normalized probability space. The primary anchor dominance primitive introduces scalar metrics—size, color, position, motion—to quantify dominance over secondary elements. These metrics form a kernel in GSE’s state transition space, enabling dynamic prioritization. The attention competition model formalizes how multiple UI elements vie for focus using a competitive matrix C_ij. This model supports both GSI's Bayesian inference of user intent and GSE's reactive state management. Failure occurs when attention is not concentrated, leading to suboptimal decision-making. Dualities emerge in the trade-off between perceptual salience and cognitive load, where increasing dominance may reduce usability. The system's robustness depends on maintaining a strict hierarchy that prevents entropy in attention allocation.
